title: The Ultimate Top 50 Films A Comprehensive Ranking

commenti.body:
You of course know that objectivity is impossible in rating art so I won’t go over arguments that you’ll hear a million times.

Instead I’ll note that, even ignoring the objectivity conversation, what you’ve made here is at most a list of the best *most popular* films. Many masterpieces are quite underseen, not easily accessible and not easily digestible for the average moviegoer.

this sounds like a fun experiment, I'm sure you had a blast compiling it and maybe made you discover a number of films you didn't know about, good for you.

BUT you earnestly touting this as "an objective, data-driven list of the greatest films ever made" makes you sound like you don't understand cinema OR data science, at all.

[They Shoot Pictures Don’t They](https://www.theyshootpictures.com/gf1000.htm) uses a methodology like this, but with a lot more lists. I like this list because there are a lot of more obscure films and films that I have overlooked.

Hon— this is a bit neat, but it’s not objective in any way whatsoever. You’re ignoring bias in data itself which is going to skew towards English language films, skew towards major films that had wider audience, and if we’re being honest skew towards a very white and male base of reviewers particularly with more internet user generated content. 

So you end up with a few things there: 

A film like Harlan County, U.S.A. Is never going to end up being on this list despite being one of the greatest documentaries ever made and being an amazing film. Despite there being a few popcorn films there, something like Titanic doesn’t end up hanging despite its high critical praise and popularity. There is literally no Spike Lee film on this list which is bananas, but makes sense with the data you’re pulling from. 

It’s a fun thing to make, but if you really want to be into data then always recognize that datapoints themselves can be biased or contaminated.
You can have objectively bad art/cinema but you'll never see it on a Hollywood scale. I've seen someone film without realising the lense cap was on. Now *that* is objectively bad.
